About Us:

Spectrum Killian (SK) is a nationally recognized leader in restorative dentistry, passionate about helping people smile with confidence. We partner with dental professionals across the country to deliver world-class restorations, advanced dental equipment, and trusted services that make a difference for patients every day.

At SK, we combine craftsmanship, cutting-edge technology, and a deep commitment to quality to create beautiful, lasting results. More than just a dental lab, we are driven by the belief that every restoration represents a person’s confidence, comfort, and well-being - and that’s a responsibility we take to heart.

Our operations are centered around two advanced Centers of Excellence located in Orange County and Los Angeles. This collaborative environment allows our skilled technicians to innovate, mentor one another, and consistently deliver outstanding results.

Overview:

At Spectrum Killian, we’re raising the standard in restorative dentistry through exceptional craftsmanship, cutting-edge technology, and trusted partnerships. We are seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Data Analyst
to own day-to-day reporting and analytics for our commercial and operations teams.

Reporting to the Senior Data Analyst, this role builds, maintains, and enhances the reports and dashboards our sales, account management, production, and engineering teams rely on every day, serves as the first responder for data requests across the business, and turns that data into insights operations and sales leaders can act on. The ideal candidate is AI-native and comfortable using Claude (Cowork and Code) to automate work and pull data, backed by strong Excel fundamentals with working SQL and Python, and communicates clearly with nontechnical partners in a fast-paced, agile, and growing dental lab.

What You'll Be Responsible For:

Build, maintain, and enhance the recurring reports and dashboards used daily by sales, account management, production, and engineering.
Serve as the first responder for day-to-day data requests across the business, with a tracked turnaround commitment.
Use modern AI tooling to automate recurring analyses and reporting, and query our cloud data lake with SQL.
Deliver account-level sales reporting, territory views, and at-risk account alerts for the account management team, and implement enhancements to our CRM.
Develop cost and performance reporting for operations: labor, materials, remakes, and on-time delivery.
Analyze sales, cost, and production trends to surface insights and recommendations that operations and sales leaders can act on.
Build and refine production and operational reporting, including live floor-performance displays at production workstations.
Validate and reconcile data across our business systems; investigate data-quality issues and resolve them at the source.
Document reporting logic, data definitions, and standard procedures.
Partner with Customer Experience, Production, Finance, Sales, and Shipping to keep information accurate and decisions data-driven.
Handle confidential customer, employee, and business information with discretion.

Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Data Science, Mathematics, Business, Information Systems, Finance, Operations, or a related field preferred.
Two or more years of experience in analytics, reporting, or a related role.
Strong communication with nontechnical stakeholders, including the ability to translate analysis into plain language, walk operations and sales leaders through the numbers, and present findings people can act on.
Strong attention to detail and a demonstrated ability to maintain accuracy while managing a high volume of information.
Hands-on comfort using AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, or similar) in everyday analytical work.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including formulas, filters, sorting, pivot tables, and lookup functions.
Working knowledge of SQL and comfort writing queries against a relational database.
Working knowledge of Python for analysis and automation (pandas, scripts, or notebooks); experience with a BI tool is a plus.
Familiarity with Git and GitHub, including version control basics and collaborating on shared code.
Experience or coursework with databases, ERP systems, CRM platforms, manufacturing systems, or other business software.
Ability to analyze information, recognize patterns, and identify discrepancies.
Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritize competing deadlines.
A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset and willingness to investigate issues through resolution.
Experience in dental, healthcare, manufacturing, laboratory, or medical-device environments is helpful but not required.

What Success Looks Like:

Day-to-day data requests are handled reliably, and data is presented clearly to nontechnical stakeholders.
Account management and sales teams have current reporting, account health views, and at-risk account alerts.
Operations leaders use cost dashboards (labor, materials, remakes, on-time delivery) every day.
Core operational reporting is live and trusted, including floor-performance displays at every production workstation.
Data-quality issues are fixed at the source, documented, and stay fixed.
Processes become more standardized, efficient, and scalable as Spectrum Killian continues to grow.

We value diversity and are committed to creating a welcoming workplace for individuals of all backgrounds.
Career Growth:

Description

The Opportunity

Prime Residential is looking for a Property Operations Analyst to join the team at Park La Brea, a 4,249-unit community in Los Angeles and one of the largest properties in our West Coast portfolio.

As Property Operations Analyst, you help leaders at Park La Brea understand operational results, spot variances, and act on key property operations priorities, including revenue, occupancy, delinquency, work orders, purchase orders, controllable expenses, and other above-the-line operating metrics. Reporting to the VP, Property Management, you own the variance analysis for property operations: identifying where results differ from expectations, following up on the drivers, and explaining what is behind them across operating metrics.

You will partner closely with Property Management, Property Accounting, Asset Management, and Centralized Services to interpret reported results, pinpoint operational drivers, and ensure timely follow-up on items that affect property performance. In short, you are the operations-focused partner who turns property activity and reported results into clear variance explanations, practical follow-up, and actionable insight for operational leaders.

What You Will Do

Own property operations KPI variance reporting for Park La Brea across revenue, occupancy, delinquency, work orders, purchase orders, and controllable expenses, with clear commentary on actual results versus budget, forecast, and prior period.
Analyze above-the-line operating results, identify variances and trends, and explain the drivers to the VP, Property Management and the operations management team.
Research material variances with operations leaders, property team members, Property Accounting, and Centralized Services to identify root causes and required follow-up, and distinguish accounting close items from operational performance drivers.
Support monthly operating reviews with variance schedules, trend summaries, and follow-up items, and track operational and capital project spend against budget, flagging risks or overruns early.
Prepare and support property budgets and periodic forecasts, gathering operating assumptions, validating inputs, and tying variance explanations back to current and expected property performance.
Own the accuracy of pre-bill each cycle and of utility billing, validating charges with property operations and the third-party utility provider before they reach residents.
Support resident ledger accuracy, delinquency tracking, Final Account Statements, and the Centralized Services collections handoff, researching and resolving discrepancies with property management and accounting.
Ensure the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of financial and operational data, and manage confidential information with discretion and integrity.

Requirements

2+ years of experience in property operations, financial analysis, resident accounting support, property management, or a related field.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills (modeling, pivot tables, lookups) and strong overall MS Office proficiency.
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills with high attention to detail.
Effective communication skills (oral, listening, and written) and the ability to present operational and financial information clearly to finance and non-finance partners.
Ability to prioritize, multitask, and meet recurring reporting deadlines, with discretion and integrity in handling confidential financial information.
Valid driver’s license for the purpose of operating a community or company vehicle.
Authorized to work in the United States.

Preferred

BS/BA degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
Experience with property management / accounting software (e.g., RealPage, Yardi).
Multifamily real estate or property operations experience.
Experience building dashboards or automating recurring reporting.
Experience with resident accounting, billing, or collections (accounts receivable) in a multifamily or property-operations setting.

About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

About The Role

Peraton is seeking a Technical Project Manager to support the day-to-day program management, scheduling, reporting, and coordination activities of the BASIS program. Working under the direction of the Program Manager, the selected candidate will assist in managing cost, schedule, and technical performance across the program's broad portfolio of application sustainment, modernization, and security activities.

This role is ideal for an early-to-mid career project management professional with a strong technical aptitude and an interest in growing within a large-scale Federal IT program. The Technical Project Manager will support Agile sprint coordination, assist in maintaining an Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), prepare status reports and briefings, track risks and issues, and serve as a coordination point between technical teams, subcontractors, and Government stakeholders. A Public Trust clearance or the ability to obtain one is required.

This is a 100% remote role.

Program & Schedule Management

Support the Contract Program Manager in managing cost, schedule, and technical performance across all BASIS program tasks and subtasks.
Maintain and update the Service Now Project schedules Server and SharePoint repository, ensuring tasks, milestones, estimated dates, and dependencies are current and provide weekly IMS presentations to customer.
Assist in developing and maintaining the Project Management Plan (PMP), Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), Product Roadmaps and Communication Plan.

Reporting & Meeting Support

Prepare weekly IPR slide decks and written reports, due 2 hours prior to each Integrated Progress Review; capture and distribute meeting minutes and action items.
Coordinate and track project deliverables

Risk & Issue Management

Support the maintenance of the formal Risk Register, including probability/impact assessments, mitigation strategies, and current status.
Coordinate with the cybersecurity team to ensure POA&M submissions and updates are completed within required timelines.
Maintain product backlog and project tasks in JIRA;

Agile & DevSecOps Coordination

Support the program's Agile/Scrum delivery model by coordinating sprint planning, daily scrum facilitation, sprint reviews, and retrospectives across technical delivery teams.
Track and report sprint point burn rates and velocity metrics.
Coordinate with QA, development, and security teams to ensure Agile sprint deliverables - including automated test cases, RTMs, and release artifacts - are on track for end-of-sprint completion.
Assist in scheduling and coordinating code reviews

Stakeholder & Subcontractor Coordination

Serve as a coordination point between internal technical teams, subcontractors, Government stakeholders, and external partners.
Assist in coordinating distribution of release notes and technical documentation.

Tools & Administrative Support

Maintain and organize program documentation, deliverable tracking, and collaboration workspaces in SharePoint.
Support reporting and data extraction activities as directed by the Program Manager.
Coordinate ServiceNow workflow tickets and incident tracking as required by program operations.

Qualifications

2 years with BS/BA; 0 years with MS/MA; 6 years with HS Diploma
Must be a US Citizen
Ability to obtain Public Trust clearance
Experience in project coordination, project management, or program support roles, preferably within IT or software development programs.
Working knowledge of project management fundamentals including schedule management, risk tracking, status reporting, and stakeholder communication.
Familiarity with Agile/Scrum methodologies and experience supporting sprint-based delivery teams.
Proficiency with project management and collaboration tools including Microsoft Project, Service Now, SharePoint, and JIRA.
Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to prepare clear, concise status reports and briefing materials for Government and senior leadership audiences.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent tasks, track deliverable deadlines, and escalate issues in a timely manner.
Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, cross-functional DoD program environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or active pursuit; Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) accepted.
SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework) or equivalent Agile certification.
Prior experience supporting DoD or Federal government IT programs with formal deliverable obligations.
Experience with DevSecOps program environments and sprint-level project tracking.
Familiarity with ServiceNow for workflow and incident management.
Experience coordinating with subcontractors and managing multi-vendor program environments.
Familiarity with DEERS, TRICARE, or other DoD healthcare/benefits systems.

Ride BART to a satisfying career that lets you both: 1) make a difference to Bay Area residents, and 2) enjoy excellent pay, benefits, and employment stability. BART is looking for people who like to be challenged, work in a fast-paced environment, and have a passion for connecting riders to work, school and other places they need to go. Who May Apply

All current BART employees and Future BART employees

Current Assignment

The San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit District (BART) is seeking an experienced Project Manager, Construction, to lead key internal efforts. BART is undertaking a significant portfolio of infrastructure renewal and expansion projects, including systemwide facilities modernization, traction power and train control upgrades, station improvements, and major maintenance facility construction. This position offers the opportunity to manage complex, high-visibility public infrastructure projects that directly support safe, reliable transit service for the Bay Area.

The incumbent will manage one or more construction projects from design coordination through construction completion and closeout. This includes developing and monitoring project budgets, schedules, risk factors, overseeing contractor and consultant performance, and ensuring compliance with contract requirements and District standards. The role also involves coordinating closely with engineering, operations, and safety divisions, and serving as the primary point of contact for project stakeholders. Current priorities include aligning schedules and budgets with District capital planning goals, enforcing rigorous contract administration, and supporting safety-critical construction in an active transit environment. Coordination between design, construction, and operations remains a priority to minimize service impacts. The position also requires regular field presence, including nights and weekends, to monitor construction progress, address field conditions, and verify compliance with plans, specifications, and safety requirements. The ideal candidate will play an integral role in advancing BART's capital investment strategy while upholding the District's commitment to safety, fiscal accountability, and community service.

The Most Qualified Candidates For This Position Will Have Highly Developed Competencies In The Following Areas, Which Will Be Reinforced With Related Work Experience And Articulated During The Selection Process

Managing construction projects in an active, operating transit or heavy civil infrastructure environment.
Administering construction contracts, including:
Development of scope
Change order negotiation and claims resolution
Reviewing BART Change Orders (CO), Change Notices (CN), and Pre-Negotiation Plans (PNP) for conformance with the RE Manual

Coordinating design and construction activities among multiple engineering disciplines and stakeholders.
Reviewing plans, specifications, and cost estimates for completeness and compliance with applicable codes and standards.
Communicating effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, including public agencies and internal departments.
Familiarity with BART Facility Standards (BFS) and the BART Resident Engineer Manual (Book 325) is preferred.

Application & Selection Process

. Applications must be completed in full and include all requested information, including dates of employment, positions held, hours worked, and a detailed description of duties performed.

Applicants may attach a resume to provide supplemental information; however, the resume does not substitute for completing the application form in its entirety. Only information included in the application at the time of submission will be used to determine whether applicants meet the minimum qualifications for the position. All application materials must be submitted by the closing date and time listed on the job announcement. Applications received after the closing deadline will not be considered.

Applicants who require assistance with the online application process may contact the Talent Acquisition Division
at (510) 464-6112 or employment@bart.gov .

The selection process for this position may include one or more of the following: a skills or performance demonstration, written examination, and/or panel or individual interview.

All applications will be reviewed by the Talent Acquisition Division to determine whether applicants meet the established Minimum Qualifications (MQs). Applicants who meet the MQs may be referred to the hiring department for further evaluation as part of the selection process.

The selected candidate must demonstrate a work history reflecting reliability and dependability and may be required to provide copies of certificates, diplomas, or other documentation required by law, including proof of authorization to work in the United States.

Pre-employment processing will include a background check. This requirement does not apply to current full-time District employees unless the position requires additional evaluations or clearances.

Examples of Duties

Coordinates and supports project team on design and construction efforts.
Develops and directs the implementation of goals, objectives, policies and procedures in assigned project areas. Administers and ensures conformance to District policies and procedures.
Plans, organizes, assigns, reviews and evaluates the work of assigned District and contract staff; manages and directs the work of contract consultants.
Directs or participates in the preparation and review of designs, plans, specifications and cost estimates; ensures specifications and contract requirements comply with District standards and policies.
Identifies equipment or systems needs on assigned projects; evaluates functional requirements; reviews vendor and manufacturer design and specifications on project equipment and materials; coordinates equipment procurement and testing activities; oversees equipment installation.
Oversees contractor and consultant contracts; develops scope of work; prepares request for proposal; reviews proposals and makes recommendation on selection; assists in contract negotiation and preparation; monitors work activities to ensure compliance with contractual obligations.
Performs construction project management duties; prepares cost estimates; prepares and monitors project schedules and budgets; conducts field inspections as required; monitors work in progress; writes, approves, negotiates and executes contract changes; authorizes contract payments upon project completion.
Serves as the project liaison with other divisions, departments and outside agencies; negotiates and resolves project issues.
Provides responsible staff assistance for higher level management staff on projects and related matters. Provides periodic status reports on budget, schedule, and issues to various departments or entities requiring information.
Attends and participates in professional group meetings; stays abreast of new trends and innovations in the field of engineering design and construction.

Experience

Five (5) years of full-time verifiable professional in construction contracts and administration, project management or related experience.

Substitution

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Blackstone Talent Group, an award-winning technology consulting and talent agency is seeking a Senior Program Manager, Enterprise AI to join our Client's team.

About The Role

We are seeking a highly accountable and execution-focused Senior Program Manager, Enterprise AI to lead delivery of our Enterprise AI portfolio. This high-impact individual contributor role translates AI strategy into measurable business outcomes.

You will lead complex, cross-functional initiatives; establish governance and operating discipline; manage risks and dependencies; and drive alignment across AI Engineering, Business Technology, business stakeholders, and executive leadership. Success requires strong program leadership, technical fluency, business acumen, and the ability to influence without direct authority.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Enterprise AI roadmap and integrated program plan, including priorities, scope, milestones, resources, dependencies, risks, decisions, and outcomes.
Translate strategic objectives into executable workstreams with clear owners, delivery plans, and measurable success criteria.
Drive AI initiatives from planning through development, launch, adoption, stabilization, and value realization.
Establish program governance, decision forums, communication rhythms, and executive reporting.
Partner with AI Engineering, architects, business teams, and leadership to align technical delivery with business priorities.
Identify early warning signals, delivery risks, resource constraints, and ownership gaps; drive issues to resolution and escalate when needed.
Remove cross-functional barriers and facilitate timely decisions across a complex, matrixed organization.
Maintain visibility into program health, critical path activities, commitments, and dependencies.
Track adoption, business impact, and realized value after launch.
Continuously improve program management practices as Enterprise AI capabilities mature.

Required Qualifications

8+ years of experience leading complex enterprise technology, digital transformation, data, analytics, or AI programs.
Proven success delivering large-scale, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through implementation and adoption.
Advanced program and portfolio management skills, including roadmap planning, governance, risk management, dependency management, and executive reporting.
Demonstrated ability to influence teams, drive accountability, and deliver results without direct authority.
Strong understanding of enterprise technology and modern software delivery practices.
Working knowledge of artificial intelligence, machine learning, Generative AI, large language models, AI agents, data, APIs, integrations, and AI-enabled applications.
Ability to partner effectively with engineers and architects and evaluate technical dependencies, risks, and tradeoffs.
Strong business acumen with the ability to connect technology investments to measurable business outcomes.
Excellent problem-solving, stakeholder management, executive communication, and decision-making skills.
Ability to create structure, urgency, and momentum in fast-paced and ambiguous environments.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with enterprise AI governance, responsible AI, security, privacy, compliance, or model risk.
Experience driving AI adoption, organizational change, training, or enablement programs.
Experience in enterprise software, cloud technology, SaaS, or contact center environments.

Security Clearance Required: N/A

Blackstone Talent Group is a wholly owned subsidiary of Blackstone Technology Group, a global IT services and software firm that implements technological solutions across commercial industry verticals and the US Federal Government. Blackstone's global talent augmentation practice was founded in 1998. Blackstone Talent Group has offices in San Francisco, Denver, Houston, Colorado Springs, and Washington, DC. We specialize in providing clients the best talent across a variety of industries and sectors.
